newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico bankers say not worried by left's rise.
newsitem.headline: Mexico bankers say not worried by left's rise.

text.p: Recent election successes by Mexico's main left-wing party do not represent a threat to the country's banks, the president of the Mexican Banking Association (ABM) said.
The left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) has seen its support rise around the country over the past year, notching up a series of advances in local elections.

Polls currently put its national strength at around 21 percent ahead of congressional elections on July 6, and PRD candidate Cuauhtemoc Cardenas leads polls to win the July 6 election for mayor of Mexico City.

Asked whether the PRD's advance was a threat, ABM president Antonio del Valle said: "I definitely feel not, first because if they win it's through democracy, but the country is very balanced and that won't change."

Del Valle, who is also president of Grupo Financiero Bital, dismissed talk that a PRD victory in the Mexico City mayor's race would delay or put off bank investment projects or lending, which collapsed after the December 1994 peso crisis. He predicted lending should pick in the second quarter of this year now that "interest rates are reasonable" and said rates would continue to fall as inflation comes down.
